summary: Concurrent XFRM route lookups update the same policy lifetime use_time field from independent WireGuard handshake workers.

call_chain.evidence: KCSAN reports this function as both write sites and xfrm_policy.ll defines it.

thread_b.role: concurrent XFRM policy lookup from worker

call_chain.evidence: The second KCSAN stack is another wg-kex worker reaching the same XFRM lookup.

interleaving: Worker A performs an XFRM route lookup and obtains a shared xfrm_policy pointer in pols[i].
Worker B performs the same lookup for the same policy.
Both workers store a new lifetime use_time value; the fix marks the benign concurrent store with WRITE_ONCE.

ground_truth_access.required_ordering: Concurrent policy lifetime timestamp updates are intentionally racy but must be marked as single-copy stores.

vulnerability_surface.why_relevant: use_time is a mutable lifetime timestamp embedded in shared xfrm_policy objects returned by lookup and updated by every successful policy use.

aliases.name: pols[i]->curlft.use_time
aliases.evidence: pols is filled from xdst->pols or lookup output before the update loop.

aliases.name: xdst->pols[i]->curlft.use_time
aliases.evidence: The function copies policy pointers from an existing bundle into pols.

thread_a.evidence: The function iterates over num_pols and updates each policy lifetime.

thread_b.evidence: KCSAN shows two wg-kex workers writing the same address.

published_by: XFRM policy tables and bundle lookup

coverage.analysis_conclusion: The reported and patched accesses are the policy use_time stores inside xfrm_lookup_with_ifid; WireGuard files explain the observed worker caller but not the access surface.

patch_hunks: de5724ca38fd wraps the use_time store in WRITE_ONCE in xfrm_lookup_with_ifid.
indirect_edges: KCSAN stack shows wg_packet_handshake_send_worker -> WireGuard send helpers -> ip6_dst_lookup_flow -> xfrm_lookup_route -> xfrm_lookup_with_ifid.
